newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian new crop conditions good.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian new crop conditions good.

text.p: Australian new wheat crop conditions were good overall with reasonable subsoil moisture levels in New South Wales (NSW), Queensland and Western Australia, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said.
The few areas still requiring more moisture were west of Walgett in NSW and in some southern pockets of NSW, it said in its weekly grain market report.
Most of the Victorian and South Australian crop was planted but Victoria's Millawa region and small pockets of South Australia's grain belt north of Port Augusta still needed planting rain, it said.
Growers appeared to be waiting for the end of the financial year, on June 30, as well as on clear indications of the effect of the El Nino weather pattern.
Both were dampening consumer activity, the AWB said.
Milling and feed grain markets were quiet this week with domestic end users in milling wheat largely covered and tonnage into the market low, it said.
Low grower selling and a reasonable level of tractor activity could be keeping stock on farm, it said.
In the feed grain market, sorghum remained the focus for Australia's east coast with central Queensland harvesting and the southern Queensland and northern NSW harvest almost completed, it said.
Brisbane, Newcastle and Sydney consumers found sorghum the cheapest grain for volume while in Melbourne sorghum sales have been significant.
Dairy demand continued in Victoria in a generally stabilising market, it said.
